intro:
Use it for a few actions on the same thing, such as archiving, snoozing or reporting one message, so they read as one control rather than a row of separate buttons.

The group sets whatever is placed directly inside it in one track, drawn like the segmented [Tabs](/docs/web/components/tabs): outline and ghost buttons lie flat with muted labels, and the one under the pointer rises out of the track. Put `Button`s in it, and an `Input`, `Menu.Trigger` or `ButtonGroup.Text` beside them.

For a split button, put a `ButtonGroup.Separator` between two filled buttons. The group then drops its track and joins them edge to edge.

To choose one option from a few, use [Tabs](/docs/web/components/tabs): a button group runs actions and does not keep a selection.

parts.Separator: Turns the group into a split button: no track, and the children joined edge to edge. Before a primary, secondary or destructive button it takes that button's fill and draws a short line in its text colour, so the two halves read as one. It runs upright by default; pass `orientation="horizontal"` in a vertical group. It is hidden from assistive technology.
parts.Text: A cell that is read rather than pressed: a prefix such as `https://`, a unit, or the value a pair of buttons changes. `size` matches the height of the `sm`, `md` or `lg` buttons and fields beside it.

examples.title: Orientation
examples.description: `orientation="vertical"` stacks the children in a column track, for map controls or a short list of options. Every child takes the width of the widest.

examples.title: Sizes
examples.description: The group has no size of its own. Give every button in it the same `size`, and the matching `size` to any `ButtonGroup.Text`.

examples.title: Split button
examples.description: A main action with a [Menu](/docs/web/components/menu) of other ways to take it. The two halves are filled, so a `ButtonGroup.Separator` divides them; give the menu's icon button an `aria-label`.

examples.title: Toolbar
examples.description: A group whose children are groups spaces them apart, one track each. Use one inner group per kind of action, each with its own `aria-label`.

examples.title: With a field
examples.description: An `Input` in the group takes the room the buttons leave, so give the group a width with `className`. Here, a search field with its button and an invite field with its action.

examples.title: Text cells
examples.description: `ButtonGroup.Text` puts fixed text on either side of a field, here a site address, or between two buttons, here the count they change.

notes:
### Accessibility

The group has `role="group"`. Give it an `aria-label` that names what its actions have in common, such as "Formatting" or "Message actions", so a screen reader announces it on the way in. Each icon-only button needs its own `aria-label` too.

The buttons stay separate stops in the tab order. The group does not move focus between them with the arrow keys.

### What takes part

Only outline and ghost buttons lie flat in the track. A field or a filled button keeps its own surface, so it reads as raised from the start.

Only direct children take part. Wrap a button in another element and that element takes its place, so the button keeps its own look. `Menu.Trigger` with `render={<Button />}` renders the button itself and joins as one.

### Server Components

It holds no state, so a Server Component can render it.
